# numpy/scipy/osqp are pinned because the surface panel is built by a
# quadratic program: a newer solver stack reproduces the pipeline but shifts
# the panel by ~1e-12 and the projected surfaces by ~1e-8 (the float32 storage
# floor). Those pins are the combination under which every table in the paper
# was regenerated byte-identically. Relaxing them is safe if you only need the
# results to agree to ~8 significant figures.
numpy==2.4.6
scipy==1.17.1
osqp==1.1.3
pandas>=2.1
matplotlib>=3.8
tabulate>=0.9
exchange_calendars>=4.5

# pandas parquet engine; the weekly 16-name study reads the IvyDB pull as
# parquet and pandas has no built-in reader
pyarrow>=15.0

# REQUIRED, not optional. The scenario covariance is a Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage
# estimate; scenarios.shrunk_cov silently falls back to a fixed 0.85/0.15
# blend if scikit-learn cannot be imported. That fallback runs to completion
# without warning and reproduces the pipeline but not the reported numbers
# (the draws move by ~6e-4, which is enough to change the adaptive-conformal
# learning rate selected on the development period).
scikit-learn>=1.3

# Results were produced with numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 / osqp 1.1.3 /
# pandas 2.2.3 / scikit-learn 1.9.0 on Python 3.14, and verified to be
# bit-identical under numpy 2.5.2 / scipy 1.18.0 on Python 3.12.
